descriptors.definition: An obligation represents a duty or responsibility that an entity has no practical ability to avoid and is owed to another party. Such duties can arise from contracts, legislation, customary practices, or published policies.
exclusion: Voluntary actions easily avoided without penalty
Duties not owed to external parties
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from contingent events where no current unavoidable duty exists.

descriptors.definition: This condition requires that an obligation possesses the potential to force the entity to transfer an economic resource under at least one circumstance. The probability of the transfer occurring can be low while still meeting the definition.
inclusion: Obligations to deliver goods or services
exclusion: Duties that never require transferring economic value under any circumstance
nearby_distinctions: Differs from actual settlement, which removes the obligation entirely.

descriptors.concept_name: Present obligation as a result of past events
descriptors.definition: A present obligation exists when an entity has already obtained economic benefits or taken specific actions, resulting in a future requirement to transfer an economic resource. The obligation can exist even if enforceability or payment is deferred to a future date.
inclusion: Liabilities arising from received goods or services
Obligations from operating in a specific market
exclusion: Obligations for unperformed contracts where no benefits have been received
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from future commitments where neither party has performed.

descriptors.concept_name: Aspects Which Are Common To Assets And Liabilities
descriptors.definition: Common structural aspects govern both assets and liabilities regarding how they are classified, aggregated, and evaluated in financial statements. These principles guide the selection of appropriate units of account and the evaluation of contractual terms.
exclusion: Specific measurement formulas for individual asset classes
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on shared architectural definitions rather than element-specific recognition rules.

descriptors.definition: The unit of account defines the specific right, obligation, or group of them to which recognition and measurement criteria are applied. It is selected to provide relevant information and faithfully represent the economic substance of transactions.
exclusion: Arbitrary groupings that obscure economic substance
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from reporting line items by its specific application to recognition and measurement.

descriptors.definition: An executory contract is a contract or portion where neither party has performed obligations or both have performed to an equal extent. It establishes an interdependent, combined right and obligation to exchange economic resources.
inclusion: Partially fulfilled contracts with equal execution
exclusion: Contracts where one party has fully performed its side of the bargain
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standalone assets or liabilities because rights and obligations are inextricably linked.

descriptors.concept_name: Substance of contractual rights and contractual obligations
descriptors.definition: Financial statements must report the underlying economic substance of contractual terms rather than merely their legal form. Explicit and implicit terms are evaluated, while terms lacking any discernible economic effect are disregarded.
inclusion: Combined effect of multiple linked contracts
exclusion: Options lacking practical ability for exercise
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts economic substance with strict adherence to legal contract phrasing.

descriptors.definition: Equity claims represent the residual interest in an entity's assets after deducting all liabilities. They encompass all claims against the entity that fail to satisfy the strict definition of a liability.
exclusion: Obligations meeting the criteria for liabilities
Contributions from equity holders treated as liabilities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from liabilities by representing residual claims rather than unavoidable economic resource transfers.

descriptors.definition: Income comprises increases in assets or decreases in liabilities resulting in equity increases, excluding equity holder contributions. Expenses comprise asset decreases or liability increases resulting in equity decreases, excluding equity holder distributions.
exclusion: Transactions involving contributions from or distributions to equity holders
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from equity movements caused by direct capital contributions or dividends.

descriptors.definition: Recognition is the capture of an element-compliant item for inclusion in the balance sheet or statement of profit and loss. The carrying amount reflects the monetary value at which the asset, liability, or equity is recorded.
inclusion: Simultaneous recognition of income and expenses
exclusion: Matching costs as a primary overarching objective
nearby_distinctions: Differs from disclosure in the notes by directly entering the financial statement totals.

descriptors.definition: Elements meeting the basic definitions are recognized only if recognition generates useful information comprising relevance and faithful representation. Judgment is required based on individual facts and circumstances to determine if non-recognition paired with note disclosures is preferable.
inclusion: Items meeting element definitions that yield relevant and faithfully represented data
exclusion: Items failing to provide useful insights even if they meet basic element definitions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from mere element definitions by adding a utility threshold for financial statement inclusion.

descriptors.definition: Recognition may fail to provide relevant information when the existence of an asset or liability is uncertain or when the probability of economic benefit inflow or outflow is low. Such uncertainties require careful evaluation alongside other factors to determine appropriate reporting.
exclusion: Certain obligations with high inflow or outflow probability
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from measurement uncertainty by questioning whether the item actually exists or occurs.
